convention: RESOLVED: the FAO 1952 "population" series is FIVE DISTINCT INDICATORS sharing one item code (r_fao_population_1952_10_18): "population total", "population agricultural", "population agricultural ocupati[on]" (economically active in agriculture) and its male/female splits. Layer B keeps them apart in the `indicator` column; the item code does not, so any median keyed on `item` alone MIXES all five and lands somewhere between them. "population total" IS true total population and can be used as such. A figure around a third of the total is the agricultural-occupied indicator, NOT a defect and NOT evidence of a territorial mismatch. Always read `indicator` before using a figure. Separately, 21 of the 212 entities carrying a total-population row have an implausible 1937->1951 step (extraction defects: Afghanistan 1951 = 0, Pakistan 1951 = 5,842k against 66,009k in 1937, Austria 1951 = 916k), so check per-entity plausibility.
evidence: Measured 2026-08-14 against consolidated_layer_b.parquet (868 fao1952 population rows, years 1937 and 1951). Yugoslavia 1937: total 15,722k (1931 census 13.9M, 1948 census 15.77M), agricultural 10,629k, agricultural-occupied 5,083k -- the previously recorded "median ~5.08M" is EXACTLY the agricultural-occupied row, and also the median of the five indicator-mixed 1937 rows the evidence bundle saw. Turkey: total 16,823k (1937) and 20,935k (1951), matching the 1935 and 1950 censuses; the recorded "~6,086k" is exactly the median of Turkey's ten indicator-mixed rows, (5,712+6,459)/2 = 6,085.5. Saar 1937 = 821k is the "population total" indicator under country label "Saar"; the Saar's agricultural rows sit under a SEPARATE label "France  Saar", so that bundle only ever saw the total series -- there was never a contradiction, and the "small/non-agricultural territory" hypothesis is falsified. The claimed uniform ~1/3 cross-check also fails: agricultural-occupied/total in 1937 is USA 6.5%, Germany 12.4%, Japan 20.2%, and the source carries NO USSR population row at all (its aggregate is literally labelled "GENERAL TOTAL EXCLUDING THE USSR"). Independent check of the total series, 1937: Italy 42,372k, France 41,200k, Egypt 16,008k, India 304,333k, China 452,460k, Poland 31,600k, USA 128,961k -- all within a few percent of accepted figures; 191 of 212 entities show a plausible 1951/1937 ratio.
verified_by: issue-13 re-measurement (indicator column resolves the apparent contradiction)

convention: IIA labels its Soviet series "Russian Federation" / "Russia" but reports WHOLE-USSR territory, not the RSFSR proper. Route to the USSR-scope polity; check magnitudes before ever routing such a label to a Russia-proper polity.
evidence: Cotton lint ~796k ha and cotton seed ~1.5M ha medians (1922-1940) are far too large for the RSFSR alone (Soviet cotton was grown in Central Asia and Transcaucasia); rye ~22M ha is union-scale.

convention: For pre-1945 years IIA's "south korea" label covers the WHOLE Korean peninsula (Japanese Chosen) — no separate southern entity existed. Anachronistic label, peninsula-scale data.
evidence: 432 dated rows 1909-1945 with peninsula-scale magnitudes; consistent with the IIA's colonial-era Korea coverage.

convention: juan reports Finland on the settled post-1940 reduced-territory basis throughout 1941-1960 — it does NOT switch to the briefly recaptured Karelia borders during the Continuation War.
evidence: Sown-area series (barley/oats/wheat) smooth and continuous across 1941-1944 and the 1944 armistice; oats fall 472k ha (1939) to a 310k ha trough (1945) then recover — wartime disruption, not a territorial step.

convention: The juan/Mitchell-FAO compiled crop-area (and likely production) series under the label 'Czechoslovakia' are reported on a roughly constant, pre-Munich/post-restoration territorial basis across 1919-1946+; they do NOT reflect the 1938-1944 wartime territorial losses (Sudetenland, southern Slovakia, occupation) that CShapes documents for polity F51-1938-1945. evidence: Direct extraction of barley and potato area (ha) by year from the juan/Mitchell-FAO source file shows smooth values across 1937-1946 (e.g. barley 671k/660k/656k/754k/647k/659k/590k/549k/550k/546k for 1937-1946) with no ~28% step change at either the 1938 or 1945 territorial-change boundaries documented in the candidate polity's wiki page.

convention: IIA figures reported under 'Djibouti'/French Somaliland for coffee, green are transit/re-export volumes of Ethiopian-origin coffee passing through the port via the Djibouti-Addis Ababa railway, not domestic production of the territory.
evidence: Web research: the Djibouti-Addis Ababa railway (1897-1917) made Djibouti the premier export port for Ethiopian coffee from the Harar region; France held a near-monopoly on Ethiopia's export trade via this route until the mid-1950s. Magnitude (median 14,114 t/yr) is implausible as domestic output for a small arid territory with no known coffee agriculture.
